Using bayesfoRest with bayesmeta

Source: vignettes/bayesmeta.qmd

bayesmeta fits a random-effects meta-analysis by direct numerical integration rather than MCMC, so there’s no sampling to configure and fits are close to instantaneous. It’s always a random-effects model – there’s no common-effect option within bayesmeta itself. Subgroup analyses, prior sensitivity, and funnel plots all work.

Fit the model

bayesmeta works from a plain vector of effect sizes and standard errors, computed with metafor::escalc(). This example uses the continuous-outcome dataset and a (raw) mean difference:

library(metafor)
library(bayesmeta)
library(bayesfoRest)

cont_es <- escalc(
  measure = "MD",
  m1i = Mean_Intervention, sd1i = SD_Intervention, n1i = N_Intervention,
  m2i = Mean_Control, sd2i = SD_Control, n2i = N_Control,
  data = cont_outcome) |>
  dplyr::mutate(sei = sqrt(vi))

model_bayesmeta <- bayesmeta(
  y = cont_es$yi,
  sigma = cont_es$sei,
  labels = cont_es$Author,
  mu.prior.mean = 0, mu.prior.sd = 1,
  tau.prior = "uniform")

tau.prior accepts several built-in non-informative priors ("uniform", "Jeffreys", "DuMouchel", and others – see ?bayesmeta::bayesmeta) or your own prior density as an R function. mu.prior.mean/mu.prior.sd set a normal prior on the pooled effect; leave them unset for an (improper) uniform prior.

Create the forest plot

bayes_forest() takes the study-level data separately from the fitted model, so pass the original cont_outcome data frame with the arm-level means/SDs, not the escalc() output:

bayes_forest(
  model = model_bayesmeta,
  data = cont_outcome,
  measure = "MD",
  studyvar = Author,
  yearvar = Year,
  mean_ctrl = Mean_Control,
  mean_int = Mean_Intervention,
  sd_ctrl = SD_Control,
  sd_int = SD_Intervention,
  n_ctrl = N_Control,
  n_int = N_Intervention,
  xlim = c(-8, 3)
)

Subgroup analysis, overall plot, and prior sensitivity

Subgroup refits work the same way as brms: subgroup = TRUE, subgroupvar = Subgroup refits bayesmeta per subgroup automatically.

overall_plot(incl_mu_prior = TRUE, incl_tau_prior = TRUE) reads the priors directly from the model (via model$mu.prior/model$tau.prior) the same way it does for brms – no need to re-specify them.

bayesmeta also supports the full bf_*() prior-sensitivity workflow (sensitivity_plot(), ecdf_model_plot(), ecdf_prior_plot()), refitting the model under each prior you specify. See vignette("brms") for a worked sensitivity example and vignette("sensitivity-analysis") for the full walkthrough – the calls are identical, just swap in a bayesmeta model.
